init.title: 1FuseLoader options
init.description: Tune thresholds. Current settings are checked together before saving. Unused phases stay at 0 A. TTL values are seconds; Easee receives rounded-up whole minutes. {error} Current decreases immediately. Fast recovery is on by default: while physically charging, current can rise directly to buffered available capacity after fresh, coherent grid/EV reports. Startup, restart delay and protective reductions still apply. Turn fast recovery off to use the gradual 1 A ramp and its timers. The minimum-current reserve applies at the configured minimum current; the normal buffer applies at higher charging current. Experimental timed overload is off by default. When enabled, the minimum current may continue above the fuse rating within a cumulative budget, after a separate short response window. These settings do not establish the installation's allowable overload or replace physical protection. Short dips, setting changes and restarts do not replenish the budget. There is no automatic budget reset. Start New Overload Trial (7 A) records a new explicit period at 7 A, at most 29 A total and at most 1800 cumulative seconds above 25 A. Two verified checkpoints are required; the vehicle must already be charging with healthy normal-load measurements. The button sends no charger command. Historical exposure and failures remain. Restart, reset, source or policy changes interrupt the period; it never resumes automatically. This is not a fuse temperature model. The start/restart setting is the minimum buffered capacity needed to begin. Once stable, the offer follows verified available capacity up to the configured car maximum, including while waiting for the vehicle. A read-only current/status refresh may be requested when newer evidence is needed for an increase. It is not a short current pulse and does not resume a manual pause or override a vehicle schedule. Conservative import fallback is off by default. Enable only after verifying that grid and car use the same L1 and that the installation has comparable importing loads without generation, storage or cancelling current. It can only retain or reduce an accepted positive cap without subtracting EV current; it grants no extra overload budget. Observation timestamps and HTTP receipts are tracked separately. Telemetry-stop recovery uses a bounded start offer rather than repeated high-current starts. Bounded nominal reduction is a separate opt-in, off by default. With the experimental profile enabled, an accepted higher cap may be reduced to startup current inside one fixed response window even when an old response latch or spent budget blocks continued overload. New physical response evidence is required; otherwise 0 A is requested and retries are limited. This never replenishes the budget. The ten-second bound applies to local decisions; the cloud API and minimum one-minute TTL cannot guarantee physical response within that time.

data.increase_stable_seconds: Gradual mode: stable headroom before increasing (seconds)
data.increase_interval_seconds: Gradual mode: interval between 1 A increases (seconds)
data.overload_margin_amps: Experimental sustained overload above main fuse (A, maximum 4)
data.overload_transition_limit_amps: Experimental peak limit during response window (A, maximum 38)
data.overload_response_seconds: Experimental response window after requesting minimum current (seconds, maximum 10)
data.fast_recovery: Fast headroom recovery (fresh, coherent current reports)
data.nominal_import_only_fallback: Conservative reduction with delayed EV data (verified import-only supply)
data.bounded_nominal_shedding: Bounded lower-current trial after overload lockout (explicit opt-in)
